block.comment: Purpose: Read one text note from MELODY.TXT into a variable and play it. Only the current line occupies RAM. Hardware: use Connections to check pin ownership for your selected board. Open the comment bubbles on the main steps for explanations.
Declare one passive buzzer and its output pin. Use its name in later blocks. The AVR engine generates sound with Timer2 and supports up to three independent voices.
Put MELODY.TXT in the SD root. Each line is a note and milliseconds, e.g. C4 250 or R 100. Open once, read only. Existing files are never overwritten.
True when the most recent operation on this card succeeded. Check it before using data from a read or continuing a file write.
Read just one bounded line into a local variable. It can also come from EEPROM read text. Do not read another note until busy is false.
True when the most recent operation on this card succeeded. Check it before using data from a read or continuing a file write.
Pass the record unchanged, e.g. F#5 250. Playback starts and returns immediately. The next loop waits for busy to become false. Blank/comment-only lines produce no sound.
Play only a complete successfully read record. EOF or an overlong line makes OK false, so the loop stops reading.
Evaluate the condition first. Execute the enclosed actions only when it is true; otherwise skip them or use the else branch.
Repeats until power is removed. Each block runs in order, then execution returns to the top. Keep this loop responsive when servicing motors, music or serial input.
